newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwanda seeks improved transit trade with Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda seeks improved transit trade with Tanzania.

text.p: Landlocked Rwanda has asked neighbouring Tanzania for improved terms for its transit trade, a senior official at the Tanzania Harbour Authority said on Tuesday.

Authority spokesman Franklin Mziray said Rwanda had sought five changes to the agreement on transit trade goods, including permission to open a Rwandan office for transit trade coordination in Dar es Salaam.

Other requests include a waiver on a mandatory deposit of $2,000 for Rwandan-bound containers, the removal of bonds on Rwandan goods and the provision of exclusive or "block" rail services by the Tanzania Railways Corporation for Rwandan goods.
The corporation's chief commercial manager, Rukia Shamte, said the request to operate block trains would be implemented immediately.
Rwanda wants Tanzania to take responsibility for direct delivery of imported goods to the Rwandan inland port of Isaka where customs documentation could be processed, said Mziray.

Rwanda currently uses two transit corridors to import and export goods. They are a northern route via the Kenyan port of Mombasa and through Uganda, and a southern corridor through Tanzania's Dar es Salaam port.

In 1996 a total of 83,000 tonnes of Rwanda-bound imports and 800 tonnes of exports, were handled by the Tanzania Harbour Authority through Dar es Salaam port. This represented 5.69 percent of total port through-put for the year. In 1995, the figure was 96,500 tonnes of imports and 6,000 tonnes of exports.
